title: The Royal Rivalry, Episode 4: The Storm Sorceress (full episode)
series: The Royal Rivalry (Clash of Clans fan comic), full episodes

lines: Previously, on The Royal Rivalry. The Warden woke up. A goblin ran off with a dragon scale, and left a map behind.
And far beyond the hills, a castle made of storm opened its eyes.
By morning, the storm castle was gone. But everyone had seen it.
The whole kingdom crowded into the Town Hall. Which still smelled a little bit of burnt curtains.
Listen to me. All of you. The Storm Sorceress has woken up.
The one from the bedtime stories?
The bedtime stories left out the worst parts.
Then we march out today, and knock her castle down.
It's made of clouds. What are you going to knock?
Very hard. I'll knock it very hard.
Nobody is marching anywhere. She wants our Elixir. So we guard the Elixir.
I'll do it. I'll guard the storage. Personally. Day and night.
Everybody thought that was very brave of the Wizard.
At noon, the sun went out.
Not behind a cloud. It simply went out, like a candle. And the sky began to hum.
The clouds twisted, and gathered, and became a face. Enormous. Crackling. Smiling.
You have something of mine. Every drop of Elixir in this valley.
Give it back by the full moon. Or I will come down, and take it.
Is it? Ask the old man where it came from.
Everyone turned to look at the Warden. The Warden did not look at anyone.
Hello, old teacher. You look tired.
Funny. That's exactly what I said to you, once.
Teacher? What does she mean, teacher?
And these are your champions? They can't even stand next to each other.
Full moon, old man. Don't make me wait.
And just like that, the sun came back on. As if nothing had happened.
Well. That was. Hm. I'll go and check on the Elixir.
That evening, the Healer found the Warden alone, staring at the Eternal Tome.
She was my student. The brightest I ever had. A long, long time ago.
I taught her everything I knew. And then I made a mistake.
The kind you don't get to take back.
And that was all he would say.
The full moon was three nights away. The kingdom had never worked so hard.
The Barbarians piled stones. The Archers fletched arrows. Nobody complained. Well. Hardly anybody.
The Barbarians built a catapult, to throw rocks at dragons. They tested it on the first rock they found.
The rock went straight up. And then, straight back down.
Wizard! Any news about the weather for the full moon?
Clear skies. Not a single cloud.
We should meet the dragons outside the walls. Head on. Charge!
We should put every archer on the towers, and let the dragons come to us.
They argued for an hour. Then the Warden made the decision for them.
King, you guard the gate. Queen, you take the towers. And the Wizard keeps the Elixir.
And try not to shoot each other.
Down in the square, the Barbarian and the Archer from the day before were sharing lunch again.
If a dragon comes, I'll protect you.
If a dragon comes, I'll be on a tower. Shooting it. Protecting you.
On the second night, the Queen spotted something on the wall. Small. Green. Sneaking.
She fired. The arrow hit the stone where the goblin had been standing, half a second before.
He was gone. Again. But there were tiny muddy footprints, leading straight toward the gate.
The goblin was at the gate. Tonight. Why?
Nobody sneaks past a hundred archers for snacks.
On the last night before the full moon, the King walked the wall. The Queen was already up there.
She said we can't stand next to each other.
We're standing next to each other right now.
In the Healer's house, the Warden was asleep. The lightning inside him crackled, a little louder than before.
Someone was sitting by his bed. The Wizard.
Hold on, old friend. Just a little longer. I promise.
The night of the full moon came. The kingdom held its breath.
The King stood at the gate. The Queen stood on the tallest tower. And the Wizard stood by the Elixir. Very, very still.
At midnight, the moon turned blue.
And out of the clouds came three Electro Dragons. One from the north. One from the east. One from the west.
A hundred arrows flew. The north dragon roared, and swerved away from the towers.
The King grabbed a boulder the size of a cow, and threw it with everything he had.
Too low! Let me fix that.
Her arrow hit the boulder in mid air, and split it into twenty pieces. Twenty pieces, straight into the dragon.
Then, as suddenly as they came, all three dragons turned around, and flew away.
Not chased off. Not beaten. Called home. As if they had finished their job.
Three dragons! Not a single building lost!
Too easy. That was far too easy.
When they opened the Elixir storage, it was empty. Every last drop. Gone.
How? Nothing touched it! We were standing RIGHT THERE!
There's no hole. No broken wall. The lock is still locked.
I was here the whole time! I didn't hear anything. Not a sound. Nothing at all.
The Wizard looked very pale. Everyone agreed he must have had a terrible fright.
Then the King went to check the gate. And stopped.
The gate's been opened. Not broken. Opened.
So the dragons were never the attack. They were the distraction.
While we were all looking at the sky, someone opened the gate from inside, and let the Elixir walk out.
Someone in this kingdom is working for her.
Nobody said the word. But everybody was thinking it.
The Warden looked slowly around the room. At the Barbarians. At the Archers. At the Healer. At the Wizard. At the King, and the Queen.
Whoever you are. I will find you.
It was the Archers! They were on the towers, nobody was watching them!
It was the Barbarians! They had the gate!
Stop it! Both of you. Look at the gate. Look at the mud.
There they were. Tiny, muddy footprints, all around the gate.
And for the first time in a very long time, the whole kingdom agreed on something.
But the Healer wasn't listening. She was kneeling by the Elixir storage, looking at the lock.
There was a scorch mark on it. Small. Neat. The kind of mark a spell leaves.
Warden? Could you look at this?
But the Warden was already gone. Out to the gate with everybody else, shouting about goblins.
And by the time anyone thought about that lock again, the scorch mark had been wiped clean.
Far away, on a hill above the kingdom, a small green figure sat alone, holding a blue dragon scale.
The scale began to crackle. Then it began to speak.
You did well, little one. They found your map. They're blaming you for everything.
I did what you asked. Now let my Boss go.
Not yet. I have one more job for you.
The scale went dark. And the goblin, who had stolen from a hundred kingdoms, looked very, very small.
And back in the kingdom, while everyone was out hunting a goblin, the Town Hall was very quiet.
Someone walked in. Someone hung a key back on its hook. Very carefully. Very quietly.
Someone who was not a goblin.
To be continued. Who opened the gate? Tell me who you suspect, in the comments.
